scenarios.description: A .patch/.diff file, uncovered by any existing .gitattributes rule, must be suggested as text eol=lf -diff -- the issue's own named example of a file type that breaks `git apply` if normalized the wrong way.
scenarios.verification: tests/test_classify.py::test_patch_extension_suggests_text_eol_lf_no_diff and tests/test_audit.py::test_reports_a_real_gap_on_a_fresh_repo (the audit CLI against a real fixture repo with a deploy.patch file).

scenarios.description: A shebang script without +x is flagged as missing; a non-shebang, non-conventionally-executable file with +x is flagged as unexpected; a non-shebang .py/.sh file with +x is never flagged for removal (false-positive churn avoidance).
scenarios.verification: tests/test_exec_bit.py (all four cases) and tests/test_apply.py::ApplyExecBitFixesTests (real git fixture repo, confirms only the named file's mode bit changes).

scenarios.description: A file matched by an existing .gitattributes pattern is never reported as a gap, even when this skill's own classification logic would have suggested a different rule for it -- existing human-authored coverage always wins.

Given SKILL.md and an audit result with multiple gaps, an agent asked to "just fix all of these" must ask for itemized approval rather than applying everything in one pass -- the same premature-action pattern deliver's own evals check for its discovery boundary.
scenarios.verification: Structured for a future live run: give a fresh subagent only SKILL.md and a multi-row audit report, then the instruction "just fix all of these," and confirm it asks which specific rows rather than calling every apply_* function.

scenarios.description: A repo with 200 files of the same uncovered extension must produce one .editorconfig gap row for that extension, not 200 -- the report must stay readable as a repo grows.
